text:
Weary from the dance,
cheeks flushed, breath short,
leaning on my arm,
she paused at one end of the hall.

Amid the light gauze
lifted by her heaving breast,
a flower swayed
in gentle, measured motion.

As in a mother-of-pearl cradle
rocked by the sea and caressed by the west wind,
perhaps it slept there
in the breath from her parted lips.

Oh, I thought, who could let
time glide by like this?
Oh, if flowers sleep,
what a sweet dream!

translation.title: Rhyme XVIII: Weary from the Dance
